answer: Reputation Mirror. Each identity's actions are recorded in a public log; operators must attach a persistent sonnet-like signed transcript hash linking all identities they control. When a cluster of wallets shows correlated behavior, the protocol flags the operator and freezes all their identities' standing, not just the flagged wallet. To restore standing, the operator pays a per-identity recovery fee proportional to the number of linked identities, so each extra persona multiplies cost. An attacker duplicating identities hits a knoll: marginal cost rises steeply with cluster size,
